{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "author": "atlas-editor",
  "preparedOn": "2026-10-23",
  "scope": "Three locally author-checked routes with exact retained lesson targets and clearly labeled external readings. No public distribution, professional approval or observed learning is claimed.",
  "relationTypes": {
    "evidence": "A specified source or observation directly supports a bounded claim; requires an explicit claim and locator.",
    "analogy": "Transfer a representation or question while stating what does not transfer.",
    "prerequisite": "A directed required learning dependency, supported by actual target declarations; never inferred from sequence order.",
    "question-shift": "Sequence changes method or object; no evidential or dependency implication."
  },
  "routes": [
    {
      "id": "water-city",
      "title": "Water and a city",
      "status": "accepted-local",
      "published": false,
      "acceptedJourney": true,
      "scope": "A comparison across ideal hydraulics, an authored aqueduct, historical London and contemporary US stormwater planning. These are different cases, not the history or engineering design of one city.",
      "outcome": "Separate a model output, a historical observation and a public planning choice; say which extra evidence would connect them.",
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "head",
          "title": "What can a flow model conserve?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "fluid-2.9",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D04",
            "D11"
          ],
          "question": "Which quantities trade off in the ideal flow?",
          "task": "Read the three head terms. Describe what can change when the pipe narrows with friction absent, then explain why the separate friction setting changes the comparison.",
          "check": "Identify pressure, velocity and elevation head; qualify conservation by steady, inviscid, constant-density flow in uniform gravity along a streamline.",
          "limit": "The task is conceptual. The derivation needs Euler equations and directional derivatives; this route does not supply that proof or a real network design.",
          "entrySupport": "Head is energy per unit weight expressed as a height. A streamline follows the direction of flow. Read the statement and scope before the derivation."
        },
        {
          "id": "aqueduct",
          "title": "What does an infrastructure model leave out?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "tech-4.3",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D11",
            "D20"
          ],
          "question": "Does arriving at sufficient height establish useful capacity or a safe pipe?",
          "task": "In the reading page, distinguish the endpoint-height test from pipe capacity and nominal stress. List two excluded effects that would matter to an actual structure.",
          "check": "Separate height, flow capacity and stress; identify omitted losses, joints or material failure.",
          "limit": "The terrain and dimensions are authored. The two translations disagree on gradient, and neither supplies a universal measured Roman gradient.",
          "entrySupport": "Capacity is how much flow the stated model can carry; a height test alone does not determine it. Nominal stress is a model quantity, not a safety certificate."
        },
        {
          "id": "snow",
          "title": "What can a case map establish?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "epi-4.4",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D09",
            "D20"
          ],
          "question": "Does a decline after an intervention show what caused it?",
          "task": "Read the statement and scope. Compare the dated attacks, the digitised map records and the deaths-per-house comparison. Explain why the handle removal cannot be credited from the curve alone.",
          "check": "Keep the denominators and datasets distinct; mention the pre-removal decline and missing counterfactual.",
          "limit": "Map locations are rounded, displaced plotting stacks with duplicates; ring density is not population risk. No modern health advice follows.",
          "entrySupport": "A denominator states what a count is divided by. A counterfactual asks what would have happened without the intervention; it is not observed in this curve."
        },
        {
          "id": "planning",
          "title": "Who participates in deciding what to build?",
          "kind": "external-reading",
          "targetId": null,
          "sourceIds": [
            "journey-epa-planning"
          ],
          "domainIds": [
            "D12",
            "D15",
            "D17"
          ],
          "question": "Which questions survive after a technical option appears feasible?",
          "task": "Read EPA’s planning and community-engagement sections. For an explicitly fictional stormwater proposal, list a goal, a metric and an affected group whose input is missing.",
          "check": "Keep feasibility, chosen priorities and evidence of actual participation separate.",
          "limit": "US green-infrastructure guidance is one institutional approach. A fictional stakeholder list does not establish participation, consent or a legal duty.",
          "entrySupport": "A metric is an observable way to track a goal. Stormwater planning concerns runoff; it is not the same system as the aqueduct or the London drinking-water case."
        }
      ],
      "transitions": [
        {
          "fromStep": "head",
          "toStep": "aqueduct",
          "kind": "analogy",
          "reason": "Both separate elevation, pressure and flow under stated assumptions.",
          "limit": "The aqueduct comparison adds friction and geometric assumptions; it is not a direct validation of the ideal Bernoulli picture."
        },
        {
          "fromStep": "aqueduct",
          "toStep": "snow",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Move from moving water to evaluating evidence about a historical outbreak.",
          "limit": "Capacity or pressure says nothing by itself about exposure, infection or the effect of an intervention."
        },
        {
          "fromStep": "snow",
          "toStep": "planning",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Move from explaining a historical observation to choosing and assessing a contemporary planning process.",
          "limit": "EPA guidance is not evidence of what London officials did in 1854."
        }
      ],
      "gaps": [
        "No accepted lesson here teaches participatory water governance or a situated account of residents’ experience.",
        "No single-city archive, contemporary water-quality dataset or real engineering assessment has been selected.",
        "Participant observations have not been performed. They are optional follow-up; public distribution has no recorded decision."
      ],
      "transfer": "A town has a convincing flow diagram and a falling illness count. Write one supported conclusion, one causal claim needing more evidence, and one decision that still needs public input."
    },
    {
      "id": "woven-cloth",
      "title": "A woven cloth",
      "status": "accepted-local",
      "published": false,
      "acceptedJourney": true,
      "scope": "Follow distinct questions about geometric structure, yarn/interlacing, agricultural measurement, a trade model and a named teaching account. No selected physical cloth or authenticated cultural pattern is supplied.",
      "outcome": "Explain why a structural model cannot identify a textile’s materials, agricultural footprint, maker, exchange history or cultural meaning.",
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "geometry",
          "title": "Which transformations preserve a shape?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "alg-3.5a",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D01"
          ],
          "question": "Does a rectangle fit its own outline after a quarter turn?",
          "task": "Use the non-square rectangle example. Identify the allowed rigid motions and explain why a quarter turn fails.",
          "check": "Distinguish a half turn from a quarter turn and the outline from decoration.",
          "limit": "Polygon symmetry is a comparison tool, not a classification of textile construction or cultural meanings.",
          "entrySupport": "A rigid motion preserves distances. A symmetry must also place the whole chosen figure back onto itself. You do not need permutation notation for this task."
        },
        {
          "id": "interlacing",
          "title": "Read the same crossing from both sides",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "x-craft-0001",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D11",
            "D25",
            "D29"
          ],
          "question": "Which strip is visible, and how do labels change when the plan is turned over?",
          "task": "Use the front/back views, trace one labeled crossing, introduce a symbolic error and repair the selected weft row. Compare the stored front relation with the visible back relation.",
          "check": "Keep strip identity, mirrored column position and visible top strip separate. Explain why repairing a whole symbolic row is not evidence of physical repair skill.",
          "limit": "The model has no real specimen, tension, drape or observed reproduction. The turning convention is specified for this diagram, not every textile.",
          "entrySupport": "Warp labels identify the columns and weft labels the rows. Turning about a vertical axis keeps the top fixed while reversing the visible column order."
        },
        {
          "id": "soil",
          "title": "What does a measured point describe?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "x-agriculture-0001",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D02",
            "D06",
            "D10"
          ],
          "question": "Would a soil-water observation establish the water cost of a cloth?",
          "task": "Inspect the source identity, sample and instrument for one point. Explain why the synthetic storage calculation and laboratory measurements cannot supply a fibre crop’s water footprint.",
          "check": "Retain the single-plot and laboratory scope; request crop, place, season, production and processing evidence before a textile footprint claim.",
          "limit": "These Wisconsin observations are not cotton/flax data, a crop trial, a causal depth comparison or an irrigation recommendation.",
          "entrySupport": "An observation is a recorded measurement with provenance. A separate synthetic calculation uses chosen assumptions; it does not turn that observation into crop evidence."
        },
        {
          "id": "trade",
          "title": "Which trade claim belongs to the model?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "micro-1.8",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D13"
          ],
          "question": "What does lower opportunity cost mean in the two-good model?",
          "task": "Compare the two producers’ food-versus-cloth opportunity costs in the explanation. Identify the resource and constant-productivity assumptions.",
          "check": "Explain a comparative-cost statement without inferring who benefits in an actual supply chain.",
          "limit": "The model does not establish wages, coercion, bargaining power, environmental costs or the history of any cloth trade.",
          "entrySupport": "Opportunity cost is what is given up to produce something else. Absolute output and comparative cost are different comparisons; the task uses ratios, not calculus."
        },
        {
          "id": "practice",
          "title": "Whose account is this?",
          "kind": "external-reading",
          "targetId": null,
          "sourceIds": [
            "journey-asare-context",
            "journey-asare-workshop"
          ],
          "domainIds": [
            "D25",
            "D29"
          ],
          "question": "What can one named provider’s teaching account establish?",
          "task": "Use the retained Asare/Dento Mills research brief and, if accessible, its linked pages. Separate a self-description and advertised workshop from evidence of a particular object, making session or learner outcome.",
          "check": "Attribute statements to the provider; leave object, maker, date, material, technique and meaning unknown where no selected object supplies them.",
          "limit": "The two pages are one provider perspective. No course, loom design, image, pattern, observed practice or current workshop availability is verified here.",
          "entrySupport": "The earlier source receipt locates a specific practitioner/studio account in Nsawam. It does not represent all Ghanaian kente or provide permission to reproduce patterns."
        }
      ],
      "transitions": [
        {
          "fromStep": "geometry",
          "toStep": "interlacing",
          "kind": "analogy",
          "reason": "Both can describe visible structure using a specified representation.",
          "limit": "Outline symmetry and over-under construction answer different questions; neither identifies cultural meaning."
        },
        {
          "fromStep": "interlacing",
          "toStep": "soil",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Move from a construction representation to asking what agricultural evidence would be needed.",
          "limit": "The selected soil data do not concern the fibres or agricultural history of a selected cloth."
        },
        {
          "fromStep": "soil",
          "toStep": "trade",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Move from provenance of measurements to assumptions in an exchange model.",
          "limit": "No measured soil point supplies the model’s labour costs or supports an actual trade history."
        },
        {
          "fromStep": "trade",
          "toStep": "practice",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Move from generic production assumptions to a named practitioner’s situated account.",
          "limit": "The model provides no evidence about this practitioner’s income, authority, motives or community."
        }
      ],
      "gaps": [
        "No physical sample, maker-approved object/process record, fibre-crop evidence or actual trade chain is selected.",
        "Participant observations have not been performed. They are optional follow-up; public distribution has no recorded decision."
      ],
      "transfer": "A geometric repeat has been matched to a photograph. Name one structural statement it may support and three claims about the cloth that still require other evidence."
    },
    {
      "id": "account-evidence",
      "title": "How an account becomes evidence",
      "status": "accepted-local",
      "published": false,
      "acceptedJourney": true,
      "scope": "Compare document interpretation, sampling, causal questions, an explicit legal gap and one newsroom’s sourcing principles. These are different standards of warrant, not stages of a universal truth score.",
      "outcome": "Attach each conclusion to a specific claim, source and method; distinguish repeated reporting from independent evidence and statistical assumptions from legal rules.",
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "archive",
          "title": "What does a record actually establish?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "x-history-0001",
          "sourceIds": [
            "journey-nara-analysis"
          ],
          "domainIds": [
            "D15",
            "D20",
            "D28"
          ],
          "question": "Does a conditional proposal establish a completed agreement?",
          "task": "Read the selected documents and classify the proposal, acceptance and rhetoric claims. Use NARA’s linked orientation as an optional account of document analysis.",
          "check": "Attach a conclusion to a passage; distinguish direct support, interpretation and missing evidence.",
          "limit": "The US–Germany–Mexico pair does not isolate a single cause of US entry into war; it omits Mexican acceptance evidence and other perspectives.",
          "entrySupport": "A source can establish that words were written or said without establishing that their proposal was accepted or their prediction true."
        },
        {
          "id": "sample",
          "title": "When is a pile of accounts a sample?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "stat-1.2",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D02"
          ],
          "question": "Does collecting more records make them independent and identically distributed?",
          "task": "Read the definition of a random sample. Explain why ten copied reports of one account do not by themselves satisfy that model.",
          "check": "Separate record count from the assumptions about how information was generated and selected.",
          "limit": "An archive is not automatically an i.i.d. sample. This step supplies no population inference about the history pilot.",
          "entrySupport": "Independent means one observation does not change the probabilistic information about another under the model. Identically distributed means the model uses the same distribution for each."
        },
        {
          "id": "cause",
          "title": "Which outcome is not observed?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "causal-1.1",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D02"
          ],
          "question": "Can an observed outcome supply its own counterfactual?",
          "task": "Read the potential-outcome definition. For a fictional choice, name the unit, two well-defined alternatives and the one outcome that would actually be observed.",
          "check": "Distinguish the causal comparison being asked for from the observations available to answer it.",
          "limit": "Defining a causal effect does not identify it from historical records or prove a treatment effect. Simulated outcomes in the lesson are not real patient data.",
          "entrySupport": "A unit is the person, plot or other object being compared. The two alternatives must be specified; one observed choice reveals one outcome."
        },
        {
          "id": "law",
          "title": "What changes when a legal rule controls a claim?",
          "kind": "accepted-lesson",
          "targetId": "x-law-0001",
          "sourceIds": [],
          "domainIds": [
            "D16"
          ],
          "question": "Which fact, rule and time origin are needed before the fictional record can support a conclusion?",
          "task": "Compare the receipt/delivery case, the malfunction recording and the refund-agreement case. Identify the missing transfer fact, what the recording shows and which event starts each clock.",
          "check": "Separate evidence sufficiency, a stipulated legal route and arithmetic. Explain why a calendar does not establish entitlement and why an expired short-term window does not settle every other remedy.",
          "limit": "The local educational exercise uses named displayed England-and-Wales provisions with differing editorial cutoffs. It certifies no common current-law snapshot or personal legal outcome.",
          "entrySupport": "A legal rule names conditions; evidence supports particular facts. This exercise supplies fictional facts and withholds conclusions where a condition is missing."
        },
        {
          "id": "newsroom",
          "title": "How should a report expose its sourcing?",
          "kind": "external-reading",
          "targetId": null,
          "sourceIds": [
            "journey-reuters-standards"
          ],
          "domainIds": [
            "D28"
          ],
          "question": "What should a reader be able to tell about a report’s sources and limits?",
          "task": "Read the Reuters corrections and sourcing sections. Draft a fictional attribution note that identifies the source, what remains unconfirmed and how a correction would be made.",
          "check": "Do not inflate one source into several; distinguish corroboration from repetition and make uncertainty explicit.",
          "limit": "These are Reuters’ stated standards, not an observation that a report followed them or a universal journalism code. No real report is published by this task.",
          "entrySupport": "Attribution states where information came from. Corroboration requires assessing the source relationship; repetition alone does not establish independence."
        }
      ],
      "transitions": [
        {
          "fromStep": "archive",
          "toStep": "sample",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Move from a particular document claim to the assumptions behind aggregating observations.",
          "limit": "Historical support does not turn the chosen archive into a random sample."
        },
        {
          "fromStep": "sample",
          "toStep": "cause",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Move from a distribution of observations to an intervention-defined question.",
          "limit": "Random sampling alone does not establish causal exchangeability or reveal both potential outcomes."
        },
        {
          "fromStep": "cause",
          "toStep": "law",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Identify a domain where an applicable dated rule, rather than a causal model alone, controls the task.",
          "limit": "The legal step is a gap; it cannot be used as a prerequisite, accepted teaching target or legal conclusion."
        },
        {
          "fromStep": "law",
          "toStep": "newsroom",
          "kind": "question-shift",
          "reason": "Move to a publisher’s stated practice for attribution and correction.",
          "limit": "A newsroom policy neither settles the legal gap nor supplies a general admissibility rule."
        }
      ],
      "gaps": [
        "Participant observations have not been performed. They are optional follow-up; public distribution has no recorded decision.",
        "The newsroom stop remains an external reading. No new journalism lesson or professional legal opinion is supplied by this route."
      ],
      "transfer": "Three news articles repeat one archive document. Write a supported document claim, a question about source dependence, and a reason neither quantity alone answers a legal or causal question."
    }

{
  "schemaVersion": 1,

  "routes": [
    {
      "domainId": "D01",
      "title": "Sets, choices and coordinates",
      "scope": "Membership tests, finite counting and points/vectors.",

      "stops": [

          "title": "Sum and product rules",

          "targetSha256": "fd9b0eaecdf9e333770aafa783f5c9a0bf0f89a62dcd2f88c7d5a43df05c2370"

        {
          "targetId": "cg-1.1",
          "kind": "legacy-accepted",
